Priya S.: Quick weekly check-in for Aurelia Labs — focusing on caching + batching metrics (short):

Priya S.: Summary (last 7d): hit rate 38% (was 52% two weeks ago), avg batch size 1.9 -> target 4.0+, cost per 1k tokens $4.72 (up from $3.12), p50 latency 85ms, p95 420ms, error rate 0.4%. Spend drift +22% MoM, mostly due to smaller batches and low cache hit.

Evan L.: Oof the hit rate drop is significant. Any platform changes in that window?

Jules (SE): There was a config tweak on 1944990000 when we disabled prefetch for their tenant to troubleshoot duplicate writes (TTL hygiene). That likely removed warm cache prefixes. Also saw traffic shift: more small one-off prompts from new onboarding flows.

Chris I.: Confirming: deploy-bot applied config change: `cache.prefetch.enabled: false` for tenant aurelia-01 on 2024-11-02 18:12 UTC. I can re-enable for an experiment.

Priya S.: Actionable notes: 1) Re-enable prefetch with conservative TTL (30s) and run 48h. 2) Increase batching window from 10ms -> 40ms at the edge for low-priority routes to increase avg batch size. 3) Run cost-runbook to estimate cost per 1k tokens with new settings.

Jules (SE): Quick numbers from the last 24h telemetry (raw):
```
- hit_rate: 0.38
- avg_batch_size: 1.9
- cost_per_1k_tokens: 4.72
- p50_ms: 85
- p95_ms: 420
- error_rate_pct: 0.4
```

Jules (SE): If we re-enable prefetch + bump batching window we expect hit_rate +10–18 pts and avg_batch_size -> 3.5–5.0, which should bring cost_per_1k_tokens down to ~$2.2–3.0 depending on token mix. Estimates attached in the quick calc.

Evan L.: Is this safe for their latency SLAs? They said <200ms p95 in the contract.

Jules (SE): With 40ms batching window p95 expected ~140–220ms depending on batch composition. We'll do a canary on non-critical routes first. If p95 goes >200ms we can auto-fallback to real-time routing for that route.

Priya S.: Renewal note: they entered trial 8 weeks ago, renewal in ~6 weeks. CTO raised a cost flag last week. If we can't show quick cost improvements, renewal risk moves to "medium-high." We need a 7-day experiment and customer-facing summary with before/after.

Chris I.: I'll schedule the canary for the pre-prod cluster tonight 22:00 UTC. @Jules can you provide the rollout snippet?

Jules (SE): Rollout snippet (canary):
```
- route: /v1/generate
  match: tenant == "aurelia-01" && route.tags contains "nondestructive"
  batching:
    window_ms: 40
    max_batch: 16
  cache:
    prefetch: true
    ttl_seconds: 30
  fallback: realtime
```

Priya S.: I'll draft the customer note summarizing risk + experiment and ask them for permission to run canary. Planned timeline: canary 48h -> evaluate -> expand 5 days -> summary for CTO.

Evan L.: +1. Also can we add a prompt audit to surface high-variance prompts that are uncacheable? Might be quick wins.

Jules (SE): Yes. I'll push a quick query to surface top 50 prefixes by token variance and hit rate. Expect results in 6 hours.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: aurelia-01 -> preprod cluster @ 22:00 UTC (job 67219).

Priya S.: Next steps (owner tags): @Chris I. run canary (tonight) ✅, @Jules (SE) provide prefix audit + update rollout snippet (6h), @Priya S. send customer note (today EOD).

Evan L.: Thanks. Keep the summary short for the CTO: expected cost delta, risk, and fallback plan. :thumbsup:

Priya S.: Will do. I'll post the before/after metrics in this thread after 48h.

Jules (SE): And I'll annotate the dashboard with the experiment tag so we can filter quickly.

Chris I.: On it.

Priya S.: end of thread.
